In an AladinoTV interview, “Village Halloween Ritual” artistic and producing director Jeanne Fleming discussed this year’s theme, “Body & Soul,” as an invitation to step away from screens and be more present with one another.

The theme reflects a concern that so much of modern life happens through devices and virtual selves. Fleming’s message for parade night is to return to the physical world: move, dance, share the music, and connect even with people you have just met. The goal is more than a spectacle; it is a reminder that creativity and community can make everyday life feel more human.

The parade’s official theme description similarly calls on New Yorkers to reconnect body and spirit through imagination and dance. For one night, the avenue becomes a place to put phones aside, join the crowd, and experience the city together.

[{'caption': "An op-ed by @EthanMWolf, founder of @DemocraticWinsMedia: 

Democrats got walloped in 2024 and have since sought to understand why. One theory has been that Kamala Harris didn’t do enough “new media.” She didn’t go on Joe Rogan’s podcast or spend enough time in the online spaces where swing voters, young men and low-information voters increasingly get their news. There is truth to that critique. But that doesn’t mean every platform, personality or form of outreach is politically wise. Take the party’s recent flirtation with Hasan Piker.

Piker, a 34-year-old left-wing Twitch streamer, has millions of followers online. Notable progressives — including Sen. Bernie Sanders (Vermont), Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (New York), Rep. Ilhan Omar (Minnesota) and New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani — have recently sought to capitalize on his platform. The argument for engaging him, which New York Times columnist Ezra Klein recently articulated, usually goes like this: Democracy requires tough conversations. Democrats ought to engage with different voices and resist the temptation to cancel anyone. They need to expand their reach and show up in more places.

Piker certainly fits that bill, but the downside of associating with him is significant. The internet personality has described Orthodox Jews as “inbred,” said “America deserved 9/11,” asserted “Hamas a thousand times better” than Israel and called the collapse of the Soviet Union “one of the greatest catastrophes of the 20th century.” In a podcast interview with a former Obama speechwriter last week, he called the Republican Party the “biggest terrorist internationally.” Other Democrats have openly rejected his views. Democratic Rep. Ritchie Torres (New York) called Piker “the poster child for the post-October 7th outbreak of antisemitism in America.”

The congressman is right. Piker’s rhetoric, moreover, reinforces caricatures Republicans have spent years attaching to Democrats: that they are weak, anti-American, extreme and culturally alienating.

Consider how the GOP is already punishing Democratic candidates for fraternizing with Piker.

Democrats got walloped in 2024 and have since sought to understand why. One theory has been that Kamala Harris didn’t do enough “new media.” She didn’t go on Joe Rogan’s podcast or spend enough time in the online spaces where swing voters, young men and low-information voters increasingly get their news. There is truth to that critique. But that doesn’t mean every platform, personality or form of outreach is politically wise. Take the party’s recent flirtation with Hasan Piker.

Piker, a 34-year-old left-wing Twitch streamer, has millions of followers online. Notable progressives — including Sen. Bernie Sanders (Vermont), Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (New York), Rep. Ilhan Omar (Minnesota) and New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani — have recently sought to capitalize on his platform. The argument for engaging him, which New York Times columnist Ezra Klein recently articulated, usually goes like this: Democracy requires tough conversations. Democrats ought to engage with different voices and resist the temptation to cancel anyone. They need to expand their reach and show up in more places.

Piker certainly fits that bill, but the downside of associating with him is significant. The internet personality has described Orthodox Jews as “inbred,” said “America deserved 9/11,” asserted “Hamas a thousand times better” than Israel and called the collapse of the Soviet Union “one of the greatest catastrophes of the 20th century.” In a podcast interview with a former Obama speechwriter last week, he called the Republican Party the “biggest terrorist internationally.” Other Democrats have openly rejected his views. Democratic Rep. Ritchie Torres (New York) called Piker “the poster child for the post-October 7th outbreak of antisemitism in America.”

The congressman is right. Piker’s rhetoric, moreover, reinforces caricatures Republicans have spent years attaching to Democrats: that they are weak, anti-American, extreme and culturally alienating.

Consider how the GOP is already punishing Democratic candidates for fraternizing with Piker.

[{'caption': '🐻🐯💛 JANOSCH – DEINE GESCHICHTEN BLEIBEN.

Janosch ist im Alter von 95 Jahren gestorben. 😢

Gestern habe ich noch mit meinem Enkel Ben eines seiner Bücher gelesen. Heute nehmen wir Abschied von einem Menschen, der Generationen mit seinen Geschichten begleitet hat.

Janosch, mit bürgerlichem Namen Horst Eckert, hatte keine leichte Kindheit. Sie war von Gewalt und schmerzhaften Erfahrungen geprägt. Und doch schenkte er uns Geschichten voller Wärme, Humor, Fantasie und Freundschaft.

Seine Lebensweisheiten waren geprägt von tiefem Humor, Entschleunigung und einer unprätentiösen Sicht auf das Leben.

Der kleine Tiger, der kleine Bär und die Tigerente brauchten keinen großen Reichtum, um glücklich zu sein.

Sie hatten einander.

Vielleicht ist das die schönste Botschaft seiner Geschichten:

Du hast uns nicht erklärt, wie man glücklich wird. Du hast uns gezeigt, wie wenig man dafür manchmal braucht.

Janosch hat uns gelehrt, dass Freundschaft wichtiger ist als Besitz, dass Fantasie keine Grenzen kennt und dass das Glück oft dort wartet, wo wir längst zu Hause sind.

Seine Geschichten waren nie nur für Kinder. Sie waren auch kleine Lebensweisheiten für Erwachsene.

💛 Danke, Janosch. Für das Lachen, die Wärme und die Erinnerungen.

Und dafür, dass ich deine Geschichten heute noch an meinen Enkel weitergeben darf.

WHAT'S REALLY IN YOUR CHEAP COSMETICS? 😱🌍

Millions of people worldwide buy inexpensive makeup, lipsticks and skincare products from online marketplaces, discount retailers and international beauty suppliers.

But how safe are these beauty bargains?

🚨 THE RESULTS OF PRODUCT SAFETY INSPECTIONS ARE ALARMING!

In a major European customs operation in 2025, authorities inspected 5,772 cosmetic products shipped directly to consumers from outside the EU.

👉 65% FAILED TO COMPLY WITH EU PRODUCT RULES!

Inspectors identified problems including missing safety documentation, incorrect labelling and, in some cases, prohibited ingredients.

⚠️ WHAT ARE THE POTENTIAL HEALTH RISKS?

💄 HEAVY METALS: Some contaminated or illegally formulated cosmetics have contained dangerous levels of substances such as mercury or lead, which can harm human health.

🧪 PFAS: Some beauty products contain persistent "forever chemicals". Scientists continue to investigate their potential health effects, and important safety questions remain unanswered.

🦠 MICROBIAL CONTAMINATION: Poor manufacturing hygiene can allow harmful bacteria and mold to contaminate cosmetics, potentially causing skin and eye infections.

❗ LACK OF TRANSPARENCY: Missing ingredient lists and safety documentation make it harder for consumers to know what they are applying to their skin.

Not every inexpensive cosmetic is unsafe, and not every regulatory violation means a product is toxic.

But low prices must never come at the expense of human health and safety!

💔 OUR SKIN IS NOT A TESTING GROUND FOR UNSAFE PRODUCTS!

Whether we live in Europe, Asia, Africa, North America or South America, we all deserve safe products, transparent ingredients and effective consumer protection.

But low prices must never come at the expense of human health and safety!

💔 OUR SKIN IS NOT A TESTING GROUND FOR UNSAFE PRODUCTS!

Jocelyn Lopez Tabares, 15, and her 23-year-old sister were picking up last-minute accessories for their costumes Friday night at the Spirit Halloween store at the Solano Town Center in Fairfield when a barrage of shots erupted.

“I felt like I was going to die,” Lopez Tabares, of Vallejo, told the California Post. “I thought it was going to be my last time living. I didn’t want to die that way.”

The shooting, which left one person dead and six others injured, was a “targeted incident” carried out by a lone gunman, police announced. The suspect remained on the run as of Saturday afternoon.

The appellate panel on Wednesday reversed a September ruling from a Staten Island judge who said the city improperly published a supplemental roll of property information and wrongly required homeowners to apply for exemptions. The appeals judges found that the plaintiffs lacked standing because they hadn’t shown they would actually be subject to the tax.

“The petitioners did not allege for injury purposes that any bad actors have misused the information purveyed by the supplemental roll, or that the publication itself subjected them to any crime, harassment, or defined public ridicule,” the appeals court said. “The publication of the supplemental roll did not cause the petitioners any concrete or definable injury, as the roll did not ‘impose an obligation, deny a right or fix some legal relationship.’”

Staten Island Justice Wayne Ozzi twice ordered the tax rollout halted, but his decisions were both times put on hold by the appellate court. The deadline to apply for exemptions from the tax was Oct. 13.

The appellate panel on Wednesday reversed a September ruling from a Staten Island judge who said the city improperly published a supplemental roll of property information and wrongly required homeowners to apply for exemptions. The appeals judges found that the plaintiffs lacked standing because they hadn’t shown they would actually be subject to the tax.

“The petitioners did not allege for injury purposes that any bad actors have misused the information purveyed by the supplemental roll, or that the publication itself subjected them to any crime, harassment, or defined public ridicule,” the appeals court said. “The publication of the supplemental roll did not cause the petitioners any concrete or definable injury, as the roll did not ‘impose an obligation, deny a right or fix some legal relationship.’”

Staten Island Justice Wayne Ozzi twice ordered the tax rollout halted, but his decisions were both times put on hold by the appellate court. The deadline to apply for exemptions from the tax was Oct. 13.

[{'caption': '❄️ MY LATEST NEW ENGLAND SNOWFALL FORECAST FOR WINTER 2026–27

My forecast favors below-average snowfall across most of New England.

This is not a snowless-winter forecast. I expect storms and several meaningful snow opportunities. I’m questioning how often those storms will have enough cold air to remain snow from beginning to end.

WHY BELOW AVERAGE?

• NOAA expects a strong-to-very strong El Niño through January–March 2027.

• CPC favors a warmer winter across much of the interior Northeast while also showing a wetter Eastern Seaboard. Wet does not automatically mean snowy. Cold air may be the limiting factor.

• A westerly QBO combined with El Niño generally favors a stronger, more stable polar vortex. That can reduce prolonged negative-AO cold outbreaks.

• The PDO remains negative, so previous strong El Niño winters are not perfect comparisons.

• The NAO and AO cannot be predicted for the entire winter. One blocked stretch could still produce a major nor’easter and quickly change seasonal totals.

The meteorology was extraordinary:

🌬️ Cold Canadian air helped strengthen a low near Nova Scotia.
🌀 Hurricane Grace supplied tropical moisture and energy.
🛑 Powerful high pressure blocked the storm and helped drive relentless winds across the Atlantic.

The storm moved westward toward New England. Some coastal locations faced waves around 25 feet high, with storm surge 4–5 feet above normal tides. The pounding continued through multiple high tides.

Along Maine’s coast, homes flooded, beaches eroded and coastal structures suffered extensive damage. Even President George H.W. Bush’s home in Kennebunkport was badly damaged. Across the affected coastline, boats sank and thousands of lobster traps were destroyed. Total storm damage exceeded $200 million in 1991 dollars.

• 1 lb mild Italian sausage, casings removed
• 1 tbsp olive oil
• 1 large onion, diced
• 6 garlic cloves, minced
• 2 tbsp tomato paste
• 2 cans crushed tomatoes, 28 oz each
• 1 cup water, plus more as needed
• 1 tsp dried oregano
• ½ cup chopped fresh basil, plus more for serving
• Salt and black pepper, to taste
• About 9 oz oven-ready/no-boil lasagna noodles

• 1 cup grated Pecorino Romano

2️⃣ Add crushed tomatoes, water, and oregano. Simmer gently for 20–25 minutes. Stir in basil and season to taste. Keep the sauce loose and spoonable—add a splash of water if it thickens.

3️⃣ Lightly oil a deep 9×13-inch dish. Spread 1 cup sauce across the bottom. Layer dry noodles, meat sauce, mozzarella, and pecorino. Repeat for 3–4 noodle layers, finishing with sauce and cheese. Every noodle, including the edges, needs sauce covering it!

4️⃣ Cover tightly with foil, lightly oiling the underside so the cheese doesn’t stick. Set on a rimmed baking sheet. Bake at 375°F for 45–50 minutes. Check the noodles with a knife; if still firm, keep covered and bake another 10 minutes before checking again. Once tender, uncover and bake 15–20 minutes until bubbling and golden.

5️⃣ Rest 15 minutes. Finish with fresh basil, scoop out a generous portion, and grab some garlic bread for that extra sauce. 😋

Homemade meat sauce, sautéed onions, fresh garlic and basil, and layers of melted mozzarella and Pecorino Romano. Saucy, cheesy, and worth grabbing seconds. 🤤

SAVE THIS RECIPE 👇
Serves 8–10 | Deep 9×13-inch dish | 375°F

🛒 INGREDIENTS

• 1 lb ground beef
• 1 lb mild Italian sausage, casings removed
• 1 tbsp olive oil
• 1 large onion, diced
• 6 garlic cloves, minced
• 2 tbsp tomato paste
• 2 cans crushed tomatoes, 28 oz each
• 1 cup water, plus more as needed
• 1 tsp dried oregano
• ½ cup chopped fresh basil, plus more for serving
• Salt and black pepper, to taste
• About 9 oz oven-ready/no-boil lasagna noodles
• 24 oz shredded low-moisture mozzarella
• 1 cup grated Pecorino Romano

👨‍🍳 MAKE IT

1️⃣ Sauté the onion in olive oil over medium heat for 6–8 minutes. Add beef and sausage; cook until fully browned. Drain excess grease. Stir in garlic for 30 seconds, then tomato paste for another minute.

2️⃣ Add crushed tomatoes, water, and oregano. Simmer gently for 20–25 minutes. Stir in basil and season to taste. Keep the sauce loose and spoonable—add a splash of water if it thickens.

3️⃣ Lightly oil a deep 9×13-inch dish. Spread 1 cup sauce across the bottom. Layer dry noodles, meat sauce, mozzarella, and pecorino. Repeat for 3–4 noodle layers, finishing with sauce and cheese. Every noodle, including the edges, needs sauce covering it!

4️⃣ Cover tightly with foil, lightly oiling the underside so the cheese doesn’t stick. Set on a rimmed baking sheet. Bake at 375°F for 45–50 minutes. Check the noodles with a knife; if still firm, keep covered and bake another 10 minutes before checking again. Once tender, uncover and bake 15–20 minutes until bubbling and golden.

5️⃣ Rest 15 minutes. Finish with fresh basil, scoop out a generous portion, and grab some garlic bread for that extra sauce. 😋

Coalition spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Maliki announced the ballistic missile interception in a statement on X. 

Shortly afterward, he reported the interception and destruction of a drone also directed at the southern region. 

The statements form part of a pattern of repeated Houthi missile and drone launches toward Saudi territory in recent weeks.

In late October, the coalition reported intercepting multiple ballistic missiles and drones aimed at areas including the Eastern Province, Riyadh region, and sites near Mecca province. 

Saudi authorities have occasionally reported debris from intercepted projectiles causing limited damage or minor injuries, while the Houthis have claimed attacks on airports and energy infrastructure. 

The Saudi-led coalition has been engaged in Yemen since 2015 against the Houthis, who control large parts of the country including the capital Sanaa.

Congratulations to Senator-elect Peggy Flanagan, a citizen of the White Earth Band of Ojibwe in Minnesota and the first Native American woman ever elected to the United States Senate, 

A citizen of the White Earth Nation, Flanagan built her career advocating for children, working families, and Indigenous communities. Before serving as Minnesota’s lieutenant governor, she served on the Minneapolis Board of Education and in the Minnesota House of Representatives. She also led the Children’s Defense Fund–Minnesota, putting children’s well-being at the center of her work.

Her journey—from local school board member to lieutenant governor to U.S. senator-elect—is a powerful reminder that leadership begins in our communities.

Her victory marks a historic milestone for Minnesota and the nation—and gives Native children another example of what their futures can hold.

Representation matters.

A citizen of the White Earth Nation, Flanagan built her career advocating for children, working families, and Indigenous communities. Before serving as Minnesota’s lieutenant governor, she served on the Minneapolis Board of Education and in the Minnesota House of Representatives. She also led the Children’s Defense Fund–Minnesota, putting children’s well-being at the center of her work.

Her journey—from local school board member to lieutenant governor to U.S. senator-elect—is a powerful reminder that leadership begins in our communities.

Her victory marks a historic milestone for Minnesota and the nation—and gives Native children another example of what their futures can hold.

Representation matters.

The rescue was all caught on camera, and NBC6 on Friday spoke to the couple who spotted the dolphin from their balcony.

The rescue happened in North Bay Village, where the couple spotted the struggling dolphin in the water, and thanks to their quick movements, the dolphin was saved.

Ahmed Raul Perez Prieto and his wife noticed a dolphin struggling, so they launched their drone to get a closer look.

In her first public statement since the failed execution, Pike said she never contemplated a life beyond her execution date and was prepared to die in peace, but woke up alone and confused in a hospital bed.

“There hasn’t been a moment since that night when I haven’t been in pain. My body hurts. My arms hurt. My hands hurt. My throat hurts. I still struggle to speak. And the pain isn’t just physical. There is pain in my mind and in my soul,” Pike said.

She also points out that laws already on the books could have been used that night, including park closing hours after 10 p.m. and laws prohibiting illegal fireworks.

Her questions get to the heart of another concern surrounding the ordinance: Are we creating a new citywide law in response to a single event when existing laws may already provide police with tools to intervene?

Pensacola Police Chief Eric Winstrom explains why he believes officers need another tool to protect young people who may find themselves in dangerous situations.

The City Council tabled the ordinance 7-0.

The Republican Party has only the President and his policies to blame for its historic losses in the 2026 midterms.

The results of the midterm votes are still rolling in. But the rejection of the President is undeniable and uncomplicated, and it reached deep into what had long been understood as conservative territory. His party has lost its Senate race in Ohio—and looks likely to lose in Michigan—where the post-industrial economy had long supplied the symbolic heart of Trumpism. It has lost in Texas, where Democrats had not won a statewide race in more than a hundred contests, stretching back to 1994, and in South Carolina. It has lost in Iowa and in Kansas, which has not seated a Democratic senator since the Great Depression. There are counties in southwestern Kansas where Trump won two years ago by about thirty-five points—Finney County, Seward County, Ford County—that, as the tallies accumulated in the state’s U.S. Senate race, were voting narrowly for the Democrat. For a decade, the country had become used to a fixed map—blue in the cities, deep red in the outlying areas. Now there is some instability around the edges.

One specific issue, or an especially weak Republican candidate, might make sense as an explanation in particular races. But the truth is that Trump’s past two years have offered voters a menu of reasons to turn away from him. In South Texas, it might have been the cruelty of the immigration raids; in Kansas, the effect of the Iran war on diesel and fertilizer prices; in South Carolina, an especially poorly chosen Republican candidate. It’s officially that time of year again. Boston’s sunsets are now happening before 6 PM, and the days are only getting shorter as Massachusetts moves deeper into fall.

Friday, October 16, marked Boston’s last 6:00 PM sunset of the season. By Saturday, October 17, the sun was already setting around 5:58 PM, and on Sunday, October 18, sunset will be around 5:57 PM.

And it’s only going to get earlier from here.

Daylight saving time ends on November 1, meaning clocks will move back one hour and Boston’s sunsets will suddenly shift into the 4 PM hour.

For anyone commuting home from work, heading to class, or just trying to enjoy some daylight after a long day, those early sunsets are about to become a regular part of life in Massachusetts.

The good news? Sunsets will start getting later again after the winter solstice, with 6 PM sunsets returning in the spring.

Until then, get ready for leaving work when it already feels like nighttime. 🥲

Be honest, do you actually enjoy the early sunsets or are you already missing summer? 👀

Starting today, October 13, Massachusetts residents ages 75 and older who no longer drive can apply for free public transportation through the MBTA’s new Car-Free Seniors Pilot Program.

The program, announced by Governor Maura Healey’s administration, is designed to help older residents stay independent, visit family, get to medical appointments, run errands and travel around the Boston area without worrying about transportation costs.

Here’s what you need to know 👇

✅ Who’s eligible? Massachusetts residents ages 75 and older who have a Massachusetts ID card instead of a driver’s license.

✅ What’s included? Free fares on MBTA buses, subways, ferries and Commuter Rail services.

✅ How do you apply? Eligible residents can apply online or in person at the Charlie Service Center, located at 296 Washington Street in Downtown Boston.

✅ When does it start? Applications officially open October 13. Seniors applying in person can receive a temporary free-fare credential the same day, while permanent credentials will be mailed.

One important detail: This isn’t automatically free transportation for everyone over 75. Residents must meet the eligibility requirements and obtain the free-fare credential through the program.

For many older Massachusetts residents who have given up driving, this could make everyday trips around Boston and surrounding communities a lot more affordable.

Speaking at a London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE) event hosted by the Huth Initiative for a New Political Economy on 27 October 2026, said the United States and Europe must recognise that “the world as it really is right now” has changed, pointing to expanding middle classes, urbanisation and economic development across the world.

Sachs said “the idea that the United States or the West still somehow runs the show” no longer reflects current realities, warning that a failure to adapt could contribute to greater geopolitical instability. He also criticised what he described as “double standards” in international affairs, arguing that perceptions of exceptionalism can increase tensions between major powers.

A wider geopolitical reading of Sachs’ remarks reflects the broader debate over the transition from a US-led international system towards a more contested and multipolar order. 

The growth of China, India and other emerging economies has challenged longstanding assumptions about Western economic and strategic primacy, while disagreements over sovereignty, military intervention and international rules have intensified debates over the legitimacy of global leadership. 

His comments highlight the risks of misreading shifts in power, particularly as major states compete to shape the future of global governance, security and economic influence.
